sections.title: Duet and these Terms
body: Duet is an iPhone app provided by Coda Compute, Inc., doing business as Coda Health. It helps you organize health information, view changes in your records and measurements, and prepare information for your doctor. These Terms govern your use of Duet and its related services.
You must use Duet lawfully and provide information or connected-service access only when you have the right to do so.

sections.title: Eligibility and cost
body: You may use Duet only if you are at least 18 years old and live in the United States. By choosing I agree and continue, you confirm both requirements and accept the version of these Terms linked in the app.
Duet is currently offered without a subscription price or in-app purchase. Your device, internet, mobile-data, healthcare, and third-party service costs remain your responsibility.

sections.title: Not medical care
body: Duet organizes your health information and may describe a change or pattern or repeat a finding from a connected record. It does not determine what that information means medically.

Duet does not diagnose conditions, assess your personal medical risk or prognosis, determine clinical significance or urgency, identify causes or medication effects, or recommend tests, treatments, or dose changes. It does not provide medical reassurance, monitor emergencies, or replace a qualified healthcare professional.

Duet's observations and doctor summaries are for organizing and communicating information. They are not medical conclusions or recommendations, even when they suggest discussing information with a doctor.

Do not use Duet for an emergency or time-sensitive medical decision. If you think you may have a medical emergency, contact emergency services. Always seek professional medical advice for questions about diagnosis, treatment, medications, or changes in care.

sections.title: Your account
body: Duet requires Sign in with Apple. You are responsible for maintaining access to your Apple account and device and for activity under your Duet account. Do not allow another person to use your account or attempt to access another person's account without permission.
The private key used for Duet sharing remains on the registered iPhone. Replacing a lost key pauses sharing, removes old encrypted payloads, and requires fresh approval from connected people.

sections.title: Connected services
body: You may authorize Duet to read information from Apple Health, one or more Epic MyChart organizations, or another supported source shown in the app. Access is limited to the permissions you grant and the visible Duet features you request. You may disconnect a source through Duet or revoke access through the provider.

Disconnecting ends future access and refresh and removes saved provider credentials, but previously imported history and its source provenance remain in Duet until separately removed where Duet offers that control or until account deletion.

Third-party services have their own terms, availability, and data practices. Coda Health does not control those services and is not responsible for provider outages, delayed device synchronization, or information the provider does not make available.

sections.title: AI features and your choices
body: AI features are optional. Duet asks for permission once information from a connected source is available. If you choose Allow AI, Coda may use selected health facts for automatic insights and the information and notes you choose for a doctor summary. We use third-party AI services as described in the Privacy Policy. Choosing Not now keeps the rest of Duet available.

You can pause AI features or withdraw AI permission in Settings. Pausing keeps your permission so you can resume later. Withdrawing permission stops future AI processing. Neither action deletes information already in your account.

AI-generated information may be incomplete or inaccurate. Review insights, corrections, doctor summaries, exports, and sharing selections before relying on or sending them. A generated summary is not a medical record or a note written by a clinician.

sections.title: Your information and choices
body: You retain your rights in the information you provide or connect. You authorize Coda Health to use it to provide, secure, and support Duet, consistent with the Privacy Policy and your choices.
Connecting a source, using Duet, or allowing AI does not authorize product-improvement or research use. Any future program requires separate, optional permission.

sections.title: Sharing and exports
body: Duet lets you select information for another person or for your doctor. You control what you share and the destination. Coda Health cannot retract information after a recipient has viewed, downloaded, remembered, forwarded, or captured it.
Do not use sharing to harass, impersonate, deceive, or obtain health information without permission. You may stop or disconnect an active Duet sharing relationship through the app.

sections.title: Acceptable use
body: You may not interfere with Duet's security or availability, reverse engineer or circumvent access controls except where law expressly permits, introduce malicious code, use Duet to violate another person's rights, or access systems or information without authorization.

sections.title: Availability and changes

We may suspend or terminate access when required by law, needed to protect people or the service, or when these Terms are materially violated. You may stop using Duet and delete your account at any time.

Source snapshots may not reflect the latest available terminology. Duet’s own groupings and wording are separate from the original source vocabularies.

sections.title: How does Duet use AI?
body: AI is optional. After you accept the Terms and finish setup, Duet asks for your permission before any AI processing. You don't need to connect a health source first.

If you choose Allow AI, Coda uses third-party AI services for your Duet conversation, remembering what you share, check-ins and reminders you ask for, reviews of new information, insights, and summaries you prepare for your doctor. If you choose Not now, the rest of Duet still works. You can change your choice in Settings.

To do this, Duet uses what you write, its earlier replies, what it remembers about you, selected health facts, and relevant details from your connected records and the items you save in Duet. For a doctor summary, it uses only the information and notes you select.
Duet never sends these to AI services:

list: Raw health samples, ECG waveforms, or audiogram measurements.
Anything another person shares with you.

body: Anything you type or paste into the conversation is sent as you wrote it.

Duet keeps one private set of notes about what matters to you, such as your goals, preferences, circumstances, and ongoing concerns. The notes can also reflect your connected records. To correct them, tell Duet in the conversation. In a long conversation, Duet may also keep a shorter summary of what you discussed earlier.

You can pause AI in Settings and resume it later, or withdraw your permission to stop future AI processing. Neither deletes your records, conversation, what Duet remembers, insights, or doctor materials. Withdrawing can't recall information already sent.

OpenAI is our AI provider. Duet sends it information only after you choose Allow AI. Our agreement with OpenAI covers the handling of eligible health information. We turn off ordinary response storage and don't permit model training with your health information.

OpenAI may still keep limited information for abuse monitoring, legal obligations, and technical processing, including encrypted prompt caching for up to 24 hours. Our settings restrict human review. They don't guarantee zero retention or processing only in the United States.

sections.title: What happens when I connect or disconnect a source?
body: You choose Apple Health permissions by data type on your iPhone. Each MyChart organization has its own authorization and disconnect control. Connecting one doesn't give Duet access to another.
Duet keeps the source and date with your records. Information from a source may be delayed, incomplete, changed, or unavailable.
While you use Duet, it refreshes MyChart about once a day. To do this, it records when you last opened Duet. If you haven't opened Duet for seven days, automatic refreshes stop until you come back.

Disconnecting a source stops future access and updates and removes its saved credentials. It doesn't change the original source. Duet keeps the history it already imported, along with insights, doctor materials, and what it remembers, and can still use them. They stay until you delete your account. You can remove doctor materials in For my doctor.
Disconnecting MyChart in Duet doesn't confirm that Epic has revoked its authorization. To revoke access at the source, use the connected-apps controls in MyChart.

sections.title: How does sharing with another person work?
body: You choose what to share and with whom. Receiving someone's information doesn't give them access to yours. Duet has no public profiles, no contact discovery, and no automatic access to new health information.

Your iPhone encrypts a separate copy of the daily measurements you select for each person. The private sharing key stays on that iPhone. In normal operation, Coda stores and delivers this encrypted information without being able to read the shared values. We can see the accounts involved, which measurement types you share, and delivery timing.
Other health information in your Duet account doesn't have this end-to-end encryption.
Information shared with you stays separate from your own. It isn't used for your analytics, AI processing, doctor materials, personal comparisons, Apple Health, widgets, or account export.

sections.title: What do notifications show?
body: Apple delivers Duet's notifications, and they are generic. When a check-in or reminder you asked for has a reply, the alert says only "You have a new message." Notifications never include a person's name, measurement names or counts, health values, or where the information came from.

Each iPhone signed in to your account registers for notifications on its own. Check-in and reminder alerts can go to every signed-in iPhone that has notifications on. Sharing alerts go only to the iPhone that holds your private sharing key.

Signing out on an iPhone stops notifications to that iPhone. Sign out everywhere signs your account out on all devices and stops notifications to all of them. Another device may keep working for up to an hour.

sections.title: Do you use my information to improve Duet?
body: You can rate Duet's replies: a thumbs up, or a thumbs down with any of the listed reasons and an optional note. Your feedback stays in your account and is included in your export. Duet doesn't use it in its replies or in what it remembers.

To improve Duet, Coda uses only daily counts of how many people gave each rating and reason. We don't use your note or your conversation for these counts. Counts from fewer than five people are left out.

A day's counts don't change once recorded, and they are kept after you delete your account. They don't identify you. We keep these counts only in deidentified form and do not attempt to reidentify them.
We don't currently use connected health information for optional product-improvement or research programs. Connecting a source, using Duet, or allowing AI doesn't give that permission.

Any future program would ask for a separate, optional choice and use only the information it needs. It would exclude raw health samples, records, documents, Genome data, doctor PDFs, free text, and anything another person shares with you. You could withdraw without losing core Duet features, and deleting your account would remove the related information Duet holds.

sections.title: How long do you keep my information?
body: We keep your information while you use Duet, and as long as needed to meet legal obligations, protect the service, or carry out a deletion or withdrawal.

rows: Your account, health information, conversation, what Duet remembers, plans, check-ins, insights, and feedback
Until you delete your account. Pausing AI or withdrawing AI permission doesn't delete them.
History from a source you disconnect
Until you delete your account.
Doctor materials
Until you remove them in For my doctor or delete your account. Duet keeps no archive of shared PDFs.
Shared information
Until you stop sharing or delete your account.
Database backups

We back up Duet's database every day and keep the seven most recent daily backups, with seven days of recovery logs. Backups are kept for a limited time and used only for recovery. This doesn't mean every copy is gone exactly seven days after you delete your account.
Recovery records

Minimal records of a deletion or withdrawal: the account or item, the restriction, and its time. They contain no health information and are kept while an older backup could otherwise undo your choice.
Service logs

30 days for routine cloud logs, 365 days for selected security and operational records, and 400 days for required cloud audit records. Access is restricted, and health information in diagnostic logs is kept to a minimum.
Daily feedback counts
Kept after you delete your account, in deidentified form.

body: Logs aren't used as a separate health profile or research dataset.
Deleting your account can't remove copies in an earlier device or computer backup, or files you exported or sent to someone else. Those copies follow the rules of wherever they are.

sections.title: How do you protect my information?
body: We use administrative, technical, and organizational safeguards. These include encryption in transit, encrypted credentials for connected services, restricted account access, and deletion controls. No storage or transmission system is completely secure.
Duet also protects the data it keeps on your iPhone, including your measurement preferences and private sharing key.

sections.title: Information we collect
body: Coda Compute, Inc., doing business as Coda Health, provides Duet. Depending on the features you use, we collect your account details and display name, health information from the sources you connect, Genome reports you import, insights, saved doctor materials, private Moments, measurement display preferences, and sharing information. Duet also retains records and original files you previously saved; general document import is no longer available.
You choose which sources to connect. Duet reads the information you authorize and does not change records in Apple Health, Epic MyChart, or another connected health source.

We record which version of the Terms you accept and when you accept it. We also record your AI permission choice, its version, and the time of your decision. These permission records contain no health information.

sections.title: How we use your information
body: We use your information to organize your health history, calculate measurements and comparisons, provide insights, prepare summaries for your doctor, sync your account, and support sharing, export, and deletion.

AI processing is optional. Once health information is available from a connected source, Duet asks for your permission before using it with third-party AI services. Allow AI covers automatic insights and summaries you request for your doctor. Not now keeps the rest of Duet available. You can change this choice in Settings.

For insights, Duet uses selected health facts and relevant details from your connected records. It may show up to three observations or none. For doctor summaries, we use only the information and notes you select. We do not send raw health samples, ECG recordings, audiograms, workout routes, raw DNA files or genotypes, original files, or another person's shared information to AI services.
We do not sell health information or use it for advertising, credit decisions, or training or fine-tuning AI models.

sections.title: Storage and service providers
body: Duet keeps protected app data on your iPhone, including your measurement preferences and private sharing key. We use Google Cloud to provide account sign-in, host Duet's services, and store account information, health data, and temporary files. Credentials for connected health services are encrypted and held by Duet's server.
Epic provides the MyChart authorization and record access you request. OpenAI is our current AI service provider. AI features are currently turned off and require your permission before use.

Coda's agreement with OpenAI covers the handling of eligible health information. We disable ordinary response storage and do not permit model training with connected health information. Limited provider retention can still apply for abuse monitoring, legal obligations, and technical processing, including encrypted prompt-cache storage for up to 24 hours. Our configuration restricts human review but does not guarantee zero retention or processing only within the United States.

The public Duet website may collect browser, device, page-view, performance, and service-log information through its hosting and performance providers. We use it to operate and improve the website. It is not added to your Duet health profile or combined with connected health information for advertising.
Our service providers process information to provide and protect Duet. We do not permit them to use connected health information for advertising, data brokerage, or tracking you across apps.

sections.title: Connected health sources
body: You choose Apple Health permissions by data type on your iPhone. Each MyChart organization has a separate authorization and disconnect control. Connecting one organization does not give Duet access to another.
We request access for the Duet features you choose and keep the source and date with your records. Information from a source may be delayed, incomplete, changed, or unavailable.

Disconnecting a source stops future access and updates and removes its saved credentials. It does not change the original source. Previously imported history, source details, insights, and doctor materials remain in Duet until you remove them using an available control or delete your account.
Disconnecting MyChart in Duet does not confirm that Epic has revoked its authorization. Use the connected-apps controls in MyChart to revoke access at the source.

sections.title: Product improvement and research
body: We do not currently use connected health information for optional product-improvement or research programs. Connecting a source, using Duet, or allowing AI does not provide that permission.

Any future program would require a separate, optional choice and use only the information needed for that purpose. It would exclude raw health samples, records, documents, Genome data, doctor PDFs, free text, and another person's shared data. You could withdraw that permission without losing core Duet features, and account deletion would remove the related information held by Duet.

sections.title: Private health sharing
body: You choose what to share and with whom. Receiving another person's information does not give them access to yours. Duet does not provide public profiles, contact discovery, or automatic access to newly introduced health information.

Your iPhone encrypts a separate copy of the selected daily measurements for each recipient. The private sharing key stays on that iPhone. During normal operation, Coda stores and delivers this encrypted information without receiving readable shared values. We can see the accounts involved, selected measurement types, and timing and delivery information. Other health information in your Duet account does not have this same end-to-end encryption.

Apple handles Duet's push notifications. It receives your device's push token, silent background notifications, and generic alerts that ask you to open Duet. Notifications do not include a person's name, measurement names or counts, health values, or the source of the information.

Information shared with you stays separate from your own health information. It is not used for your analytics, AI processing, doctor collection, personal comparisons, Apple Health, widgets, or account export.

sections.title: Retention and security
body: We use administrative, technical, and organizational safeguards to protect your information, including encryption in transit, encrypted provider credentials, restricted account access, and deletion controls. No storage or transmission system is completely secure.

We keep account information for as long as needed to provide Duet, meet legal obligations, protect the service, or carry out a deletion or permission withdrawal. We retain minimal recovery records identifying the affected account or item, the restriction, and its time. They contain no health values or content and remain while older recoverable copies could otherwise undo your choice.

Account deletion removes your information from Duet's active account stores. Earlier copies may remain in restricted backups. We schedule daily database backups, keep the seven most recent successful backups, and retain seven days of recovery logs. Backups are used only for recovery. Keeping seven backups does not mean every copy is deleted exactly seven days after you delete your account.

Routine cloud service logs are retained for 30 days. Selected security and operational records are retained for 365 days, and required cloud audit records for 400 days. We restrict access and minimize health information in diagnostic logs. These records are not used as a separate health profile or research dataset.

Deleting your account cannot remove a copy from an earlier device or computer backup, or a file you exported to another service or person. Those copies follow the controls and retention of their destination.

sections.title: Your controls
body: You can manage connected sources, pause AI features, withdraw AI permission, export your account information, stop sharing, sign out, or delete your account. Withdrawing AI permission stops future processing but cannot recall information already sent in a request. It keeps your existing records, insights, and doctor materials.
Start fresh in For my doctor clears the note, selected items, and active summary after you confirm. Duet keeps no archive of shared PDFs.

Account deletion removes active account data, Terms and AI permission records, provider credentials, retained health information, insights, doctor materials, and sharing content. It also clears local account data and sharing keys from the iPhone. The limited backup and recovery records described above remain under their retention rules. Deletion cannot retract information another person has already received, viewed, or captured.

sections.title: Eligibility
body: Duet is available to adults age 18 or older who live in the United States. You confirm this when you accept the Terms. We do not infer eligibility from your health information, device location, or Apple account.
